papers.title: Scaffold-Constrained Generative Design Overcomes Failure Modes in Computational Protein Engineering.
papers.abstract: Applying unconstrained generative protein models to fixed structural scaffolds can produce systematic design artifacts, including glycine enrichment, grammar violations, and discordant complex predictions. We developed DARPinMPNN, a scaffold-constrained computational framework that restricts production sequence generation to permitted DARPin Greek Grammar residue pools. A state-aware chimeric multiple sequence alignment strategy supported AlphaFold2-Multimer (AF2) screening, followed by complementary AlphaFold 3 (AF3) evaluation. Of 15,000 generated variants targeting mesothelin, VEGF-A, and H
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors identify systematic failure modes that occur when unconstrained generative protein models are applied to fixed structural scaffolds, such as glycine enrichment and grammar violations. They develop DARPinMPNN, a scaffold-constrained framework that restricts sequence generation to permitted DARPin Greek Grammar residue pools, and use it to design 15,000 variants targeting mesothelin and VEGF-A, screened with AlphaFold2-Multimer and AlphaFold3. This approach overcomes the artifacts seen in unconstrained design and improves the reliability of computational protein engineering.

papers.title: What deep learning can and cannot (yet) do for enzyme design.
papers.abstract: Deep learning has substantially advanced structure-based enzyme design, yet reliably creating highly efficient enzymes remains out of reach. One emerging enzyme design strategy combines diffusion-based scaffold generation around active-site models with sequence design. Such structure-based approaches have expanded the accessible reaction space and enabled the emergence of enzymes with diverse catalytic functions and complex catalytic motifs. Despite notable catalytic efficiencies (kcat/KM), turnover rates (kcat) often remain limited, suggesting that current approaches typically yield tight sub
papers.summary: This review examines the current capabilities and limitations of deep learning for enzyme design, highlighting that while diffusion-based scaffold generation combined with sequence design has expanded accessible reaction space and produced enzymes with diverse catalytic functions, reliably achieving high catalytic efficiency remains elusive. The key bottleneck is that while catalytic efficiencies (kcat/KM) can be notable, turnover rates (kcat) often remain limited, indicating that current approaches typically yield tight substrate binding but poor product release.

papers.title: Benchmarking machine learning and molecular dynamics methods for the prediction of the thermophysical properties of organic liquids.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of thermophysical properties is crucial for the rational design of lubricants and cooling fluids. We compile a database of approximately 4700 critically evaluated reference values for the density, viscosity, and thermal conductivity of 835 unique organic molecules in the C10-C50 range. We use this database to train and benchmark a range of machine learning (ML) architectures and molecular representations. XGBoost models trained on molecular descriptors are consistently among the most accurate across all three target properties. Out-of-distribution tests show that descriptor
papers.summary: This study compiles a database of ~4700 critically evaluated thermophysical property values (density, viscosity, thermal conductivity) for 835 organic molecules in the C10-C50 range and uses it to benchmark machine learning architectures and molecular representations against molecular dynamics methods. XGBoost models trained on molecular descriptors consistently outperform other approaches across all three target properties, with out-of-distribution tests revealing limitations of descriptor-based models.

papers.title: Microbial aldehyde-alcohol dehydrogenase degrades metformin to limit therapeutic response in type 2 diabetes.
papers.abstract: Metformin is a first-line therapy for type 2 diabetes, yet therapeutic responses vary widely. Whether gut microbes directly inactivate metformin and limit its efficacy remains unclear. Here, we identify a gut microbial aldehyde-alcohol dehydrogenase, AdhE, from Eubacterium species enriched in individuals with a low response to metformin. AdhE converts metformin to pharmacologically inactive products, lowering intestinal and systemic drug exposure. Genetic deletion of AdhE or phage-mediated depletion of AdhE-producing Eubacterium hallii MD1 restores metformin exposure and glycemic control in mi
papers.summary: This study identifies a gut microbial enzyme, aldehyde-alcohol dehydrogenase (AdhE) from Eubacterium species, that directly inactivates metformin by converting it into pharmacologically inactive products. Individuals with low metformin response harbor higher levels of AdhE-producing bacteria, and deleting AdhE or depleting these bacteria via phage restores drug exposure and improves glycemic control in mice. The findings establish a causal link between specific gut microbes and variable metformin efficacy in type 2 diabetes.

papers.title: Genome-wide-scale prediction of compound-protein interactions using foundation and language models based on three-dimensional structures of compounds and proteins.
papers.abstract: The identification of compound-protein interactions (CPIs) is crucial in the early stages of drug discovery. However, machine-learning (ML)-based methods based on one- and two-dimensional representations cannot capture important geometric information on the binding sites of CPIs, which limits their predictive accuracy.
papers.summary: This paper presents a machine-learning approach for predicting compound-protein interactions at genome-wide scale by leveraging foundation and language models that incorporate three-dimensional structures of both compounds and proteins. The method aims to overcome the limitations of 1D and 2D representation-based models, which fail to capture geometric binding-site information critical for accurate CPI prediction. This could improve early-stage drug discovery by enabling more accurate large-scale screening of compound-protein pairs.

papers.title: Predicting Enzyme Turnover Numbers and Enabling Rational Enzyme Evolution.
papers.abstract: Enzyme turnover number ( k cat  ) is a central kinetic parameter for biocatalysis, but experimental determination is low-throughput and existing computational methods inadequately model enzyme-reaction interplay. Here, we introduced MCKcat, a deep learning framework that integrates multi-scale convolutional feature extraction and cross-attention to enable deep, reciprocal fusion of enzyme sequence and reaction fingerprint representations for accurate k cat  prediction. We constructed MCKcat-DB, a large-scale dataset comprising 33 396 enzyme-reaction-based k cat  data points, covering both wild
papers.summary: The authors developed MCKcat, a deep learning framework that combines multi-scale convolutional feature extraction with cross-attention to jointly model enzyme sequences and reaction fingerprints for predicting enzyme turnover numbers (kcat). They also built MCKcat-DB, a large-scale dataset of 33,396 enzyme-reaction kcat data points, and demonstrated that the model can guide rational enzyme evolution. This provides a practical tool for biocatalysis and protein engineering where experimental kcat measurement is low-throughput.

papers.title: GPCR heteromers: Beyond the monomeric paradigm in neuropsychiatric drug discovery.
papers.abstract: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) constitute the largest druggable superfamily of membrane proteins and underlie approximately 35% of all approved medicines. Yet this conventional paradigm leaves a substantial minority of neuropsychiatric patients with incomplete efficacy, treatment resistance, or dose-limiting adverse effects. Converging evidence from structural biology, single-molecule biophysics, and molecular pharmacology has dismantled the monomeric model. GPCRs function in vivo as dynamic homomeric and heteromeric complexes in brain regions directly implicated in disease, including the
papers.journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
papers.summary: This review argues that GPCRs function in the brain as dynamic homo- and heteromeric complexes rather than isolated monomers, challenging the classical drug-discovery paradigm that targets single receptors. The authors synthesize structural, biophysical, and pharmacological evidence showing these heteromers are relevant in neuropsychiatric disease regions, and suggest that targeting them could improve efficacy and reduce treatment resistance or side effects.

papers.title: A de novo GABPA Variant in a Patient with Multifocal Cutaneous Vascular Tumors of an Unclassified Entity.
papers.abstract: We investigated the genetic basis of a previously unclassified congenital vascular anomaly in a patient with multifocal cutaneous vascular tumors. Through genomic analysis, we identified a novel heterozygous de novo germline variant in GA-binding protein-alpha (GABPA), an ETS family transcription factor. Histopathologic evaluation demonstrated capillary-venous lesions lacking glucose transporter 1 expression, distinguishing this entity from common infantile hemangioma. Notably, the tumor vasculature exhibited a prominent alpha-SMA-positive perivascular cell layer, with nuclear localized GABPA
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study identifies a novel de novo germline variant in the GABPA transcription factor in a patient with multifocal cutaneous vascular tumors that do not fit any known classification. The tumors show distinct histopathology, including GLUT1-negative capillary-venous lesions and an alpha-SMA-positive perivascular layer, suggesting GABPA dysfunction underlies this new vascular entity.

papers.title: Criteria-guided selection of alternative zinc-binding groups of HDAC3 inhibitors using in silico and in vitro approaches.
papers.abstract: Histone deacetylases (HDACs) are epigenetic enzymes linked to several biological functions and diseases. Class I HDACs (HDAC1-3) share high protein sequence and active site similarity. Hydroxamate-based inhibitors, while highly potent, are non-selective with poor pharmacokinetic profile, prompting exploration of alternative zinc-binding groups. The study applied criteria-guided identification of HDAC3 inhibitors with alternative zinc-binding groups following structure-based virtual screening, with a prioritisation of HDAC3-specific binding interactions and bidentate/monodentate interaction wit
papers.summary: This study used structure-based virtual screening followed by in vitro testing to identify HDAC3 inhibitors with alternative zinc-binding groups, aiming to overcome the poor selectivity and pharmacokinetics of traditional hydroxamate inhibitors. By prioritizing interactions specific to HDAC3 and evaluating bidentate versus monodentate zinc coordination, the authors identified candidate compounds that may offer improved selectivity within the class I HDAC family.

papers.title: A water-pinning hotspot drives templated tau aggregation.
papers.abstract: Tau assembles into fibrillar aggregates that are pathological hallmarks of a group of neurodegenerative diseases collectively called tauopathies. Templated aggregation of naïve tau to seeding-competent fibrils that proceed from cell to cell is a key driver of prion-like progression of tauopathies. This study tests the hypothesis that tau, an intrinsically disordered protein (IDP), achieves in-register stacking to form seed-competent fibrils by a pinning action of tau to each other and/or the seed surface via a single dominant hotspot to avoid mismatch in tau stacking to fibrils. Structured sol
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study investigates how the intrinsically disordered protein tau achieves in-register stacking to form seed-competent fibrils, proposing that a single dominant 'water-pinning' hotspot mediates tau-tau and tau-seed interactions to prevent mismatched stacking. The findings suggest a mechanistic basis for templated tau aggregation that drives prion-like progression of tauopathies.

papers.title: Evolutionary Dynamics-Aware De Novo Design of a Thermostable NS1-Derived Diagnostic Protein for Yellow Fever Virus.
papers.abstract: Serological diagnosis of neglected arboviruses remains hindered by extensive intra-genus cross-reactivity, compromising both assay specificity and epidemiological accuracy. In this study, we focused on yellow fever virus (YFV) as a model system to design and validate a generalizable de novo protein design framework integrating evolutionary genomics with structural modeling to rationally engineer diagnostic antigens with reduced cross-reactivity and improved cost-effectiveness. Through comprehensive evolutionary mapping over time of the YFV polyprotein, we identified conserved yet discriminator
papers.summary: The authors developed a de novo protein design framework that combines evolutionary genomics with structural modeling to engineer a thermostable diagnostic antigen derived from the yellow fever virus NS1 protein. By mapping evolutionary conservation across the YFV polyprotein, they identified regions that are conserved yet virus-specific, aiming to reduce cross-reactivity with related flaviviruses in serological assays. This proof-of-concept demonstrates a generalizable approach for improving diagnostic specificity for neglected arboviruses.

papers.title: Mechanism-Driven Design of Metal-Phenolic Networks: From Precision Assembly to Multidimensional Synergistic Therapy for Brain Diseases.
papers.abstract: Background: Brain disorders, such as glioblastoma, Alzheimer's disease and ischemic stroke, represent formidable challenges due to the highly restrictive blood-brain barrier (BBB) and the complex pathophysiological microenvironment, which severely compromise drug delivery and therapeutic outcomes. Metal-phenolic networks (MPNs), as a class of novel hybrid materials, hold great promise for overcoming brain delivery bottlenecks and enabling precise synergistic therapy by leveraging their unique physicochemical properties. However, a comprehensive synthesis of MPN designs tailored specifically to
papers.summary: This review discusses metal-phenolic networks (MPNs), a class of hybrid materials, as a strategy for overcoming the blood-brain barrier and treating brain diseases like glioblastoma, Alzheimer's disease, and ischemic stroke. It synthesizes design principles for MPNs, from precision assembly to multidimensional synergistic therapy, highlighting their physicochemical properties for improved brain drug delivery.

papers.title: Pockets to products: a data-driven approach for classification of monoterpene synthases.
papers.abstract: Monoterpene synthases (mTSs) are a large family of enzymes, which have promising industrial applications, yet remain difficult to engineer due to complex and poorly understood sequence-function relationships. Here, we present a structure-based machine learning (ML) framework that accurately predicts whether a mTS is likely to produce linalool or limonene, chosen as canonical examples of linear and cyclic monoterpene products, respectively. Our approach identifies active site properties, which are used as ML features, enabling functional predictions that go beyond sequence alone. As residue pos
papers.summary: This paper presents a structure-based machine learning framework that predicts whether a monoterpene synthase will produce linalool (linear) or limonene (cyclic) by using active site properties as features rather than sequence alone. The approach addresses the difficulty of engineering these enzymes by capturing structure-function relationships that sequence-based methods miss.

papers.title: Morphology Evolution and Structural Reorganization of Enzyme-Biosurfactant Systems: Implications for Petroleum Interfacial Engineering.
papers.abstract: The escalating demand for sustainable chemical solutions in petroleum engineering has catalyzed the development of bio-based formulations characterized by high interfacial activity and low environmental toxicity. This study investigates the intermolecular interactions and structural evolution within composite systems comprising representative glycolipid biosurfactants and carbohydrate hydrolases. Rheological and light scattering assessments reveal that the introduction of enzymes triggers a transition from large-scale micelles to highly dispersed micro-aggregates, accompanied by a significant
papers.summary: This study examines how adding carbohydrate hydrolase enzymes to glycolipid biosurfactants changes the system's structure, causing a shift from large micelles to smaller, dispersed micro-aggregates. The findings suggest enzyme-biosurfactant combinations could improve interfacial performance in petroleum engineering applications.

papers.title: KAN-GIN: Adaptive Nonlinear Molecular Representation Learning for Drug-Target Affinity Prediction.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Accurate drug-target affinity (DTA) prediction supports virtual screening, lead optimization, and drug repurposing. This study investigates whether replacing the conventional post-aggregation multilayer perceptron within a Graph Isomorphism Network drug encoder with a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) transformation improves DTA prediction. Methods: The resulting KAN-GIN framework combines molecular-graph representations with a convolutional protein-sequence encoder. It was evaluated on the DAVIS, KIBA, and METZ benchmarks against a matched GIN baseline and representative
papers.summary: KAN-GIN replaces the standard MLP readout in a Graph Isomorphism Network drug encoder with a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network transformation, paired with a convolutional protein-sequence encoder, to predict drug-target binding affinity. Evaluated on DAVIS, KIBA, and METZ benchmarks against a matched GIN baseline and other representative methods, it tests whether adaptive nonlinear function learning improves affinity prediction.

papers.title: Molecular Docking of Natural Products: Critical Appraisal of Current Methodology and Practical Guidelines.
papers.abstract: Molecular docking is among the most widely used techniques in structure-based drug discovery and has become integral to natural-product research. Despite substantial advances in computational algorithms and artificial intelligence, the methodological quality of published docking studies on natural compounds remains highly variable, and generally accepted methodological guidelines have yet to be established. This review critically evaluates current approaches to molecular docking of natural compounds, examines the specific features of different natural-product classes and protein targets, and o
papers.summary: This review critically appraises current molecular docking practices for natural products, highlighting that methodological quality remains highly variable despite advances in algorithms and AI. It examines how different natural-product classes and protein targets affect docking reliability and proposes practical guidelines to standardize future studies.

papers.title: Unveiling Novel Metalloprotease Inhibitors Targeting Botulinum Neurotoxin Through Structure-Based Virtual Screening of Drug Libraries and Molecular Dynamics Simulations.
papers.abstract: Botulinum neurotoxin (BoNT) is one of the most lethal biological substances to humans, which inhibits acetylcholine release by the presynaptic nerve in neuromuscular junctions. Of the existing BoNT serotypes, BoNT serotype A (BoNT/A) is particularly potent, making it the primary focus in neurotoxin research. Its catalytic domain exhibits similar structural features and zinc-dependent activity as thermolysin, a key bacterial enzyme, which provides a foundation for designing antibacterial agents targeting related protease mechanisms. Repurposing of preapproved drugs or existing medications has r
papers.summary: This study uses structure-based virtual screening of existing drug libraries combined with molecular dynamics simulations to identify novel metalloprotease inhibitors targeting the catalytic domain of botulinum neurotoxin serotype A. The approach leverages the structural similarity between BoNT/A and thermolysin to repurpose preapproved drugs as potential therapeutics against this highly lethal neurotoxin.

papers.title: GeoEPred: A multimodal structure-aware geometric deep learning framework for Gram-negative bacterial secreted effector prediction with sequence semantics.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of effector proteins secreted by Gram-negative bacteria is important for elucidating bacterial pathogenic mechanisms and developing precise anti-infective strategies. Although existing methods have benefited from the strong sequence feature extraction capacity of pretrained protein language models, reliance on linear sequence information alone often fails to fully capture the three-dimensional conformational signals required for virulence functions. Meanwhile, conventional structure-based methods are limited by the scarcity of experimentally resolved protein structures. To
papers.summary: GeoEPred is a multimodal deep learning framework that combines protein language model sequence embeddings with predicted 3D structural features to identify secreted effector proteins in Gram-negative bacteria. By integrating geometric deep learning over structure graphs with sequence semantics, it aims to overcome the limitations of sequence-only and structure-only predictors, especially given the scarcity of experimental structures.

papers.title: Integrative bioinformatics analysis of Lianmei granules in diabetic nephropathy: Epidemiological and molecular insights.
papers.abstract: Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is a severe complication of diabetes mellitus, leading to end-stage renal disease and significant morbidity. Current therapies are limited by efficacy and side effects, highlighting the need for novel treatments. Lianmei granules (LMG) show potential for treating DN, although their mechanisms remain unclear. This study explored DN epidemiology and investigated the active components, targets, and mechanisms of LMG using a comprehensive bioinformatics approach. We conducted a cross-sectional analysis involving 44,090 participants from the National Health and Nutrition E
papers.summary: This study combined epidemiological analysis of 44,090 NHANES participants with network pharmacology and bioinformatics to identify the active components and molecular targets of Lianmei granules (LMG) in diabetic nephropathy. The authors propose candidate mechanisms and targets for LMG, though the findings are largely computational and lack experimental validation.

papers.title: Exploiting Neosartorya (Aspergillus) fischeri antifungal protein 2-defined fungal targets for drug repurposing against Candida albicans.
papers.abstract: Invasive fungal infections caused by Candida albicans remain major clinical challenges because of the limited therapeutic options, toxicity, and emerging resistance. Drug repurposing offers a promising strategy to accelerate antifungal discovery by leveraging existing compounds with known safety profiles. In this study, we applied a structure-based drug repurposing approach guided by the antifungal protein Neosartorya (currently Aspergillus) fischeri antifungal protein 2 (NFAP2), which targets fungus-specific intracellular proteins, including glutamate decarboxylase, mitochondrial ATP synthase
papers.summary: The study uses the antifungal protein NFAP2 from Aspergillus fischeri as a guide to identify fungus-specific intracellular targets, including glutamate decarboxylase and mitochondrial ATP synthase, in Candida albicans. A structure-based drug repurposing screen then leverages these targets to find existing compounds with known safety profiles that could be repurposed as new antifungals. This offers a potentially faster route to new treatments for invasive Candida infections amid rising resistance.

papers.title: The structural context of mutations in proteins predicts their effect on antibiotic resistance.
papers.abstract: In Mycobacterium tuberculosis, a prevalent and deadly pathogen, resistance to antibiotics evolves primarily through non-synonymous mutations in proteins. Sequence-based analyses can uncover the genetic basis of antibiotic resistance, but these methods focus on primary sequence and often neglect other biological signals, such as protein structural information. We hypothesize that integrating the structural context of mutations improves the prediction of effects on function and phenotype. We curate high-confidence structural annotations for the M. tuberculosis proteome from 1350 crystallography
papers.summary: This study shows that incorporating protein structural context into mutation effect prediction improves forecasts of antibiotic resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. By curating high-confidence structural annotations for the M. tuberculosis proteome from crystallography data, the authors demonstrate that structure-aware models outperform sequence-only approaches. The work highlights the value of integrating structural biology with genomics for understanding resistance evolution.

papers.title: Atomic structure and dynamics of the mechanosensitive channel MscL from Escherichia coli by cryo-EM and solid-state NMR.
papers.abstract: Mechanosensitive channels are central to cellular responses to membrane tension, yet the structural basis of their gating remains incompletely understood. Here, we determine the structures of wild-type and Gly22→Ser (G22S) mutants of MscL from Escherichia coli (EcMscL) by cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) in peptide-based lipid nanodiscs and complement them with solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) measurements in liposomes to capture their dynamics in a native-like membrane environment. The cryo-EM structures reveal a closed conformation, whereas analysis of the low-threshold G2
papers.summary: This study combines cryo-EM and solid-state NMR to determine structures and dynamics of the mechanosensitive channel MscL from E. coli in lipid nanodiscs and liposomes. The cryo-EM structures capture a closed conformation, while the G22S mutant provides insight into the low-threshold gating mechanism. The work advances understanding of how membrane tension drives channel opening in a native-like lipid environment.

papers.title: Microtubule destabilization by SB225002 through preferential weakening of lateral tubulin interactions revealed by structural and computational analyses.
papers.abstract: Microtubules are essential for cell division and intracellular signaling, making them well-established targets for anticancer therapy. However, the clinical utility of conventional microtubule-targeting agents is often limited by toxicity and drug resistance. SB225002, originally identified as an interleukin-8 receptor antagonist, has been reported to disrupt microtubule dynamics and exhibit anticancer activity with relatively low toxicity in preclinical studies. Yet, the structural basis of its interaction with tubulin remains poorly understood. Here, we determined the crystal structure of th
papers.summary: This study solves the crystal structure of tubulin bound to SB225002, a drug originally developed as an interleukin-8 receptor antagonist that also disrupts microtubules. Structural and computational analyses show that SB225002 preferentially weakens lateral interactions between tubulin subunits rather than longitudinal ones, explaining its mechanism of microtubule destabilization. This provides a structural rationale for developing lower-toxicity anticancer agents targeting microtubule dynamics.

papers.title: Fluorination: A strategy to tune the interactions of molecules and nanoscale systems with biological matter.
papers.abstract: Fluorination has become a key molecular engineering strategy in medicinal chemistry and nanomedicine, enabling the fine tuning of the physicochemical and biological properties of therapeutic molecules and drug delivery systems. The unique characteristics of fluorine, including its small steric footprint, high electronegativity, and exceptional strength of the C-F bond, enhance metabolic stability, modulate lipophilicity and acidity, and improve pharmacokinetic profiles. Beyond these well-established effects, fluorination has emerged as a tool for controlling the assembly and biological behavio
papers.summary: This review discusses how fluorination—adding fluorine atoms to molecules—has become a key strategy in medicinal chemistry and nanomedicine for tuning the properties of drugs and drug delivery systems. Fluorine's unique chemistry improves metabolic stability, lipophilicity, and pharmacokinetics, and is increasingly used to control how molecules and nanoscale systems assemble and interact with biological matter.

papers.title: Structural basis of serine protease inhibition by antibodies from biased Fab phage-display libraries.
papers.abstract: Biased Fab phage-display libraries were designed to determine whether inhibitory CDR H3 motifs from potent anti-matriptase antibodies could be transferred to target homologous serine proteases. Using reverse-binding and substrate-like H3 motifs from parental clones A11 and E2 as templates, six synthetic libraries with 1010 diversity were constructed. Selection against matriptase identified 16 inhibitors with sub-100 nM potency, representing 100,000-fold improvement over circularized H3 loops alone. Selection against TMPRSS2, a serine protease implicated in viral entry and prostate cancer with
papers.summary: This study designed biased Fab phage-display libraries to test whether inhibitory CDR H3 motifs from anti-matriptase antibodies could be transferred to homologous serine proteases. Selection against matriptase yielded 16 inhibitors with sub-100 nM potency, a 100,000-fold improvement over circularized H3 loops alone, and selections against TMPRSS2 also identified inhibitors. The work provides a structural and methodological framework for engineering antibody-based serine protease inhibitors with broad applicability.

papers.title: GNPS-assisted identification of bioactive constituents from Scoparia dulcis and their anti-inflammatory mechanisms via network pharmacology and experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Scoparia dulcis L. (SD) is an edible medicinal herb traditionally consumed as a cooling beverage in tropical Asia for the management of metabolic and inflammatory disorders; however, its dietary bioactive constituents and anti-inflammatory mechanisms have not yet been fully elucidated. In the present study, the metabolite profile of the aerial parts of SD (ASD) was characterized, and their anti-inflammatory potential was evaluated through an integrated approach incorporating LC-HRMS/MS-based molecular networking, network pharmacology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and in v
papers.summary: This study used GNPS-based molecular networking combined with network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to identify bioactive constituents in Scoparia dulcis and predict their anti-inflammatory mechanisms. Experimental validation confirmed the anti-inflammatory potential of the identified compounds, providing a mechanistic basis for the traditional use of this edible herb.

papers.title: Lipid composition-driven sorting of ABHD5 between monolayer and bilayer surfaces.
papers.abstract: Lipid droplets (LDs) are ubiquitous organelles that store neutral lipids and serve as central regulators of lipid homeostasis. Their structure includes a hydrophobic core of triacylglycerols and sterol esters surrounded by a phospholipid monolayer. This organization creates biophysical properties that guide selective protein recruitment. Among LD-associated proteins, α/β-hydrolase domain-containing protein 5 (ABHD5, also known as CGI-58) is a key regulator of lipolysis and broader lipid metabolism, yet the mechanisms guiding its distribution between endoplasmic reticulum (ER) bilayers and LD m
papers.summary: This study investigates how the lipid composition of cellular membranes directs the localization of ABHD5 (CGI-58), a key regulator of lipid breakdown, between the endoplasmic reticulum bilayer and the phospholipid monolayer surrounding lipid droplets. The authors show that differences in lipid composition drive selective sorting of ABHD5 to these distinct membrane surfaces, providing a biophysical mechanism for how proteins are recruited to lipid droplets.

papers.title: Thermal proteome profiling identifies new drug targets in Plasmodium falciparum parasites.
papers.abstract: Spreading resistance to clinically used antimalarial drugs increases the need for identification of new drug targets. Here, we screened 25 antimalarials with known and unknown mode of action to validate old and find new drug targets in P. falciparum. Combining experimental approach by proteome-wide cellular thermal shift assay and computational filtering by molecular docking, we found the drugs to bind to previously known drug targets, validated ACS10 as the target of MMV665915 and discovered new drug targets. Furthermore, we updated the experimental and analytical MS-CETSA pipeline with the i
papers.summary: This study used thermal proteome profiling (MS-CETSA) combined with molecular docking to screen 25 antimalarial drugs against Plasmodium falciparum, confirming known targets and identifying new ones, including ACS10 as the target of MMV665915. The authors also improved their experimental and analytical pipeline for detecting drug-protein interactions in parasites.

papers.title: DyME: An MD-based engine exploiting HTP mutagenesis for protein engineering and recognition mimicry.
papers.abstract: Protein recognition mimicry is of great interest in the field of molecular bioengineering and rational design, with mutagenesis frequently employed to analyze the effects of altering amino acids involved in molecular recognition. The conformational and energetic effects of such alterations can be investigated in detail with the help of molecular dynamics (MD) methodologies. While existing MD-based computational tools can be used to explore a particular set of mutations at a time, suitable for small-scale studies, high-throughput (HTP) exploration of protein recognition for engineering purposes
papers.summary: DyME is a molecular dynamics-based computational engine designed to enable high-throughput exploration of protein mutagenesis for protein engineering and recognition mimicry. It addresses the limitation of existing MD tools that can only handle small sets of mutations at a time, allowing systematic large-scale analysis of how amino acid changes affect protein recognition.

papers.title: DeepSAP: An Integrated Generative and Predictive Deep-Learning Framework for Controllable Design of Self-Assembling Peptides.
papers.abstract: Self-assembling peptides (SAPs), particularly short sequences whose amino acid composition dictates their spontaneous organisation, are emerging as versatile building blocks in biomedicine and bio-optoelectronic materials. As the thermodynamic and kinetic behaviours of peptide self-assembly are affected by intrinsic factors, such as amino acid sequence, length, and hydrophobicity, the controllable design of SAPs with tailored properties is essential to achieve specific structures and functions for various application scenarios. However, existing computational approaches, which primarily focus
papers.summary: DeepSAP is a deep-learning framework that combines generative and predictive models to design self-assembling peptides with controllable properties. It addresses the challenge of tailoring short peptide sequences for desired assembly behavior by integrating sequence generation with property prediction. This enables more targeted design of peptide-based biomaterials.

papers.title: BioForge: A Fast and Safe Macromolecular Structure Preparation Library in Rust.
papers.abstract: BioForge is the first macromolecular structure preparation library for Rust, complementing sequence-analysis libraries such as Rust-Bio with cleaning, geometry-based missing-atom repair, protonation, and solvation as a force-field-agnostic preprocessing stage. Across 22 structures (1439-3 819 839 atoms) on a single CPU core, BioForge scales linearly in wall time (fitted N0.89) versus super-linear N1.17 for PDBFixer and N1.25 for PDB2PQR, completing the 3.8M-atom 9MJN in 5.1 s at 1.1 GB peak (PDBFixer: error, 273 GB); PDB2PQR is limited to fewer than 100 000 atoms. BioForge also compiles to Web
papers.summary: BioForge is a new Rust library for preparing macromolecular structures for simulation, handling cleaning, missing-atom repair, protonation, and solvation in a force-field-agnostic way. It scales nearly linearly with structure size, processing a 3.8-million-atom structure in 5.1 seconds using 1.1 GB of memory, whereas PDBFixer failed and PDB2PQR is limited to under 100,000 atoms. It also compiles to WebAssembly, enabling browser-based use.

papers.title: Computational identification of potential inhibitors for chikungunya virus nsP2pro.
papers.abstract: Chikungunya virus remains a crucial global health issue with no approved therapy available. In particular, the viral replication is associated with the non-structural protein 2 protease (nsP2pro). In this study, possible inhibitors for nsP2pro from the National Cancer Institute (NCI) database were screened via computational approaches. Molecular docking simulations were initially predicted top potential ligands. MD simulations were then performed to refine the ligand binding pose. During the equilibrium intervals, the ligands formed rigid contacts with the residues Asn476, Ala511, Tyr512, Tyr5
papers.summary: This study used molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations to screen the NCI compound database for potential inhibitors of the chikungunya virus nsP2 protease (nsP2pro), a key enzyme in viral replication. Top candidate ligands were identified and shown to form stable contacts with key active-site residues during simulation. The work provides computational starting points for antiviral drug development against chikungunya, though experimental validation is still needed.

papers.title: Semi-Rational Design of CpNampt Mutants for Enhanced Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) Synthesis in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
papers.abstract: β-Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) serves as a direct precursor of the essential cofactor NAD⁺, playing a crucial role in regulating mitochondrial function and delaying cellular aging. Synthetic biology, with its environmental and economic advantages, has become an important approach for the production of natural medicines, with the optimized design of metabolic pathways at its core. In this study, we focused on the NMN‑consuming pathway mediated by the nma1 and pof1 genes in Saccharomyces cerevisiae and consequently generated their double‑knockout mutant, DHSX02. Futhermore, a highly efficie
papers.summary: This study engineered Saccharomyces cerevisiae to boost production of nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN), a precursor to the anti-aging cofactor NAD+. The authors knocked out two NMN-consuming genes (nma1 and pof1) and used semi-rational design to create improved CpNampt enzyme mutants, increasing NMN yield through optimized metabolic pathway design.

papers.title: Design, Synthesis, and In Vitro Evaluation of Pinostrobin-Based Hydrazones as Potent α‑Glucosidase Inhibitors.
papers.abstract: Twenty-four pinostrobin hydrazone derivatives (TN01-TN24) were synthesized through two continuous steps from pinostrobin, hydrazone, and aldehyde derivatives, well characterized and screened for inhibitory activity against yeast α-glucosidase (Saccharomyces cerevisiae). To further expand the chemical space, a QSAR-guided approach was employed, leading to the identification of four additional candidates (TN25-TN28). Eleven compounds exhibited >80% inhibition at 50 μM, outperforming acarbose, with most displaying IC50 values below 10 μM. Among them, TN27 showed the highest potency with an IC50 o
papers.summary: This study synthesized 24 pinostrobin-based hydrazone derivatives and used QSAR-guided design to generate four more candidates, then screened them against yeast α-glucosidase. Eleven compounds achieved over 80% inhibition at 50 μM, surpassing acarbose, with most IC50 values below 10 μM and TN27 being the most potent. The work identifies promising new scaffolds for α-glucosidase inhibition, relevant to diabetes management.

papers.title: Computational Design of Three-Dimensional Nitrogenated Holey Graphene Structures with Phase-Dependent Optoelectronic Properties.
papers.abstract: In this work, we propose and comprehensively characterize two novel three-dimensional nitrogenated holey graphene (3D-NHG) structures, designated as the α and β phases. These architectures are predicted through a computational protocol based on the controlled compression of stacked 2D-NHG monolayers. Their dynamical and structural stabilities are assessed via phonon dispersion calculations and molecular dynamics simulations within the density-functional tight-binding framework. Density functional theory calculations reveal that the α phase is a semiconductor with an indirect HSE06 bandgap of 0
papers.summary: This paper computationally predicts two new three-dimensional forms of nitrogenated holey graphene (α and β phases) created by compressing stacked 2D monolayers. The α phase is a semiconductor with an indirect bandgap, and the two phases show distinct optoelectronic properties, suggesting potential for tunable electronic and optical applications.

papers.title: Integrated In silico and In Vitro Evaluation of Piperine Derivatives as Potential Efflux Pump Inhibitors in Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
papers.abstract: The increasing prevalence of antibiotic resistance mediated by efflux pump activity represents a major challenge in the treatment of infections caused by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). Efflux pumps such as NorA and MepA reduce intracellular antibiotic accumulation and contribute significantly to decreased antibiotic efficacy. In this study, PBSA-7, a piperine-derived compound, was evaluated as a potential efflux pump inhibitor using an integrated in silico and in vitro approach. Computational analysis, including molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, Lipinski r
papers.summary: This study evaluates PBSA-7, a piperine-derived compound, as a potential efflux pump inhibitor against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). Using molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and in vitro assays, the authors assess its ability to inhibit NorA and MepA efflux pumps, which contribute to antibiotic resistance by reducing intracellular drug accumulation. The work suggests piperine derivatives may serve as promising adjuvants to restore antibiotic efficacy in MRSA.

papers.title: Computational Study of CO2 Capture by Metallic Nanoparticles in Diethylenetriamine Solution.
papers.abstract: The high concentration of CO2 present in the atmosphere caused by human action is triggering a series of climate disorders worldwide, such as an increase in global temperatures. Therefore, it is necessary to develop new efficient and sustainable technologies to remove excess CO2 gas from the atmosphere. Based on this problem, this work aims to investigate the action of noble metal nanoparticles contained in diethylenetriamine (DETA) on CO2 capture through computational simulations. First, platinum nanoparticles (PtNPs) and palladium nanoparticles (PdNPs) are obtained by the CHARMM-GUI server,
papers.summary: This computational study investigates how platinum and palladium nanoparticles dispersed in diethylenetriamine (DETA) solution affect CO2 capture, using molecular simulation tools including the CHARMM-GUI server to build the nanoparticle models. The work aims to identify whether noble metal nanoparticles can enhance the efficiency of amine-based CO2 absorption as a route to more sustainable carbon capture technologies.

papers.title: Opening the black box: study of the multi-target anticancer mechanisms of Ecballium elaterium cucurbitacins via in vitro, network pharmacology, and molecular docking analyses.
papers.abstract: Ecballium elaterium is a perennial plant species that belongs to the Cucurbitaceae family. In this study, we examined the biological activities and analyzed the chemical profiles of ethyl acetate, acetone, aqueous acetone, and water extracts from different parts (aerial parts, fruit peels, and seeds) of E. elaterium. We performed chemical characterization using UPLC-ESI-MS/MS. To investigate the biological activities of the extracts, antioxidant capacity, enzyme inhibition, and cytotoxicity assays were conducted. Thirty-eight compounds were detected in the extracts, and cucurbitacins and their
papers.summary: This study characterizes the chemical composition of Ecballium elaterium extracts using UPLC-ESI-MS/MS, identifying 38 compounds including cucurbitacins, and evaluates their antioxidant, enzyme inhibition, and cytotoxic activities. Network pharmacology and molecular docking analyses were then used to predict multi-target anticancer mechanisms of the cucurbitacins. The work provides a preliminary mechanistic framework linking these plant compounds to potential anticancer targets.

papers.title: The PTPN1/N2 Peptide Inhibitor Achieves Potent, Long-Acting Glycemic Control and Weight-Loss Dual Efficacy in Mice.
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus and obesity are closely linked metabolic disorders driven by insulin and leptin resistance. Current long-acting therapies capable of addressing both conditions are dominated by incretin-based agents, which primarily achieve efficacy through appetite suppression and are frequently associated with tolerability limitations and metabolic rebound after treatment discontinuation. Alternative strategies that correct underlying signaling defects without suppressing food intake remain lacking. Protein tyrosine phosphatases PTPN1 and PTPN2 act as coordinated intracellular negati
papers.summary: This study reports a peptide inhibitor targeting the protein tyrosine phosphatases PTPN1 and PTPN2 that simultaneously improves blood glucose control and promotes weight loss in mice. Unlike incretin-based drugs that mainly suppress appetite, this approach corrects underlying insulin and leptin signaling defects, offering a potentially more durable dual-action therapy for type 2 diabetes and obesity.

papers.title: ParaEM: Antigen-aware sequence-based paratope prediction with Expectation-Maximization.
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of antibody paratopes-the residues contacting the antigen-is vital for understanding antibody-antigen recognition, antibody engineering, and vaccine design. However, structure-based predictors require antibody structural inputs, which are often obtained from experimentally determined antibody-antigen complexes in benchmark settings but are generally unavailable for new sequences. Conversely, sequence-based predictors scale efficiently but remain largely antigen-agnostic, limiting their use of pair-specific antigen context.
papers.summary: ParaEM is a new computational method that predicts antibody paratopes (the residues that contact antigen) directly from antibody sequence, while incorporating antigen context through an Expectation-Maximization framework. This addresses a key gap: structure-based predictors need unavailable structural data, and existing sequence-based methods are largely antigen-agnostic. The approach aims to improve paratope prediction for antibody engineering and vaccine design.

papers.title: Network Pharmacology-Based Prediction and In Vivo Validation of Fumonisin B1-Induced Liver Injury and Early Fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Fumonisin B1 (FB1) is a widespread mycotoxin contaminating food and feed, exhibiting severe hepatotoxicity. This study aimed to systematically investigate the underlying molecular mechanisms of FB1-induced liver injury and early liver fibrosis by combining network pharmacology with an in vivo animal model. First, network pharmacology and molecular docking were utilized to screen the core targets and key signaling pathways of FB1-induced hepatotoxicity. Subsequently, an in vivo C57BL/6 mouse model was established via intragastric administration of FB1 (5 mg/kg/day for 28 days). Serum levels of
papers.journal: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology
papers.summary: This study combines network pharmacology and molecular docking with an in vivo mouse model to identify core targets and signaling pathways underlying fumonisin B1-induced liver injury and early fibrosis. The authors validate their computational predictions experimentally using C57BL/6 mice treated with FB1 for 28 days, linking the mycotoxin to specific hepatotoxic mechanisms.

papers.title: Discovery of PIM-1 kinase inhibitors from marine natural products through machine learning and structure-based screening.
papers.abstract: PIM-1 kinase, a serine/threonine kinase implicated in several cancers, has emerged as a promising yet underexplored target for anticancer therapy. This study aimed to identify the potential of PIM-1 inhibitors from marine natural products by integrating machine learning (ML)-based quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) modeling with structure-based virtual screening.
papers.summary: This study combines machine learning-based QSAR modeling with structure-based virtual screening to identify PIM-1 kinase inhibitors from marine natural products. PIM-1 is an underexplored anticancer target, and the work demonstrates a computational pipeline for discovering novel inhibitors from marine sources.

papers.title: Trypsinogen Pro-Region as a Molecular Scaffold for the Design of Competitive Peptide Inhibitors of Trypsin-Like Proteases.
papers.abstract: Soybean (Glycine max L. Merrill) productivity is severely impacted by the velvetbean caterpillar Anticarsia gemmatalis Hübner, 1818 (Lepidoptera: Erebidae), a major defoliating pest in soybean-producing regions. Current management strategies rely heavily on chemical insecticides, which are associated with environmental risks and the development of resistance. Protease inhibitors have emerged as a promising alternative, as protein digestion in lepidopteran larvae is primarily mediated by trypsin-like serine proteases. In this context, the rational design of short inhibitory peptides represents
papers.journal: Archives of insect biochemistry and physiology
papers.summary: This paper explores using the pro-region of trypsinogen as a molecular scaffold to rationally design short competitive peptide inhibitors targeting trypsin-like serine proteases in the velvetbean caterpillar, a major soybean pest. The approach aims to provide an environmentally safer alternative to chemical insecticides by disrupting protein digestion in lepidopteran larvae.

papers.title: Multidimensional molecular profiling reveals decidual and circulating NK cell dynamics in early and late pregnancy.
papers.abstract: Human pregnancy presents a unique physiological state that allows for growth of an antigenically dissimilar foetus. The immune system plays a key role in establishing and maintaining successful pregnancy, yet detailed understanding of immunological responses in pregnancy is lacking.
papers.summary: This study uses multidimensional molecular profiling to characterize natural killer (NK) cell populations in both the decidua (uterine lining) and peripheral blood across early and late pregnancy. It reveals dynamic changes in NK cell phenotypes and functions that likely support fetal tolerance and immune adaptation during gestation. The findings provide a detailed immune atlas of pregnancy-relevant NK cells.

papers.title: Identification of Crocin I as a positive modulator of GSTP1 with potential relevance to prostate cancer.
papers.abstract: Glutathione S-transferase Pi 1 (GSTP1) is frequently silenced in prostate adenocarcinoma (PRAD), yet whether its residual catalytic activity can be chemically enhanced is largely unexplored. Here, we identify Crocin I as a positive modulator of GSTP1 through structure-based screening, biophysical characterisation, and biochemical validation. Bio-layer interferometry (BLI) supported a concentration-dependent association between Crocin I and GSTP1, and enzymatic assays demonstrated enhanced catalytic activity. Michaelis-Menten kinetics showed that Crocin I increased Vmax without markedly alterin
papers.journal: Journal of enzyme inhibition and medicinal chemistry
papers.summary: This study identifies Crocin I, a natural compound, as a positive modulator that binds to and enhances the catalytic activity of GSTP1, an enzyme often silenced in prostate cancer. Using structure-based screening, biophysical binding assays, and enzyme kinetics, the authors show Crocin I increases GSTP1 activity, suggesting a potential chemical strategy to boost residual enzyme function in prostate adenocarcinoma.

papers.title: 3D CNN-CVAE and LSTM-guided de novo design of rotigotine derivatives targeting dopamine D1 and D3 receptors in restless legs syndrome.
papers.abstract: Restless legs syndrome (RLS) is a chronic neurological disorder associated with altered dopaminergic signaling, while long-term dopamine agonist therapy may be limited by augmentation and reduced clinical benefit. This study applied a three-dimensional convolutional neural network conditional variational autoencoder integrated with long short-term memory molecular generation to design rotigotine-derived candidates targeting dopamine D1 and D3 receptors. Fourteen unique derivatives were generated and screened through pocket prediction, molecular docking, interaction profiling, pharmacophore ana
papers.summary: This study uses a 3D CNN conditional variational autoencoder combined with LSTM-based molecular generation to design novel rotigotine derivatives targeting dopamine D1 and D3 receptors for restless legs syndrome. Fourteen unique candidates were generated and filtered through pocket prediction, docking, interaction profiling, and pharmacophore analysis. The work demonstrates a deep-learning pipeline for de novo drug design in a neurological context, though experimental validation of the candidates is not reported.

papers.title: Identification of flavonoids from natural products against hyperlipidaemia through computational approaches.
papers.abstract: Over the centuries, hyperlipidaemia has been recognised as a major risk factor contributing to cardiovascular disease (CVD). Current research increasingly explores natural compounds such as flavonoids for their potential lipid-lowering effects. This study evaluated pharmacological potential of flavonoids to identify strong inhibitors for target receptor, Proprotein Convertase Subtilisin/Kexin Type (PCSK9). A total of 29 compounds, including one FDA-approved drugs were screened for drug-likeness and ADMET properties, followed by molecular docking and Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations using PC
papers.summary: This study used computational methods—drug-likeness screening, ADMET prediction, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations—to evaluate 29 flavonoids and one FDA-approved drug as potential inhibitors of PCSK9, a key target for lowering cholesterol. The goal was to identify natural flavonoid compounds that could serve as leads for treating hyperlipidaemia and reducing cardiovascular disease risk.

papers.title: A dual-functional antiviral and anticancer peptide to target intricate host-pathogen interacting proteins of human papillomavirus associated with head and neck cancer.
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma is increasingly being reported worldwide, and a major contributing factor is the incidence of human papillomavirus infections. The viral infection activates proto-oncogenes and signalling mechanisms aiding in tumorigenesis. An efficient way to block the virus-induced carcinogenesis is to identify a common medicament that can effectively inhibit the viral and host proteins. In the present study, HNSCC transcriptomic profiles and HPV genes involved in host-pathogen interactions were retrieved. The overexpressed HNSCC genes were further considered for host-pa
papers.summary: The authors mined HNSCC transcriptomic data and HPV-host interaction networks to identify overexpressed host genes and viral proteins that drive HPV-associated head and neck cancer. They then designed a dual-functional peptide predicted to simultaneously target both viral and host proteins, aiming to block virus-induced carcinogenesis. This is an in silico/computational study proposing a candidate therapeutic peptide rather than experimental validation.

papers.title: An immunoinformatics-driven multiepitope subunit vaccine targeting Oropouche virus: Molecular docking, immune and dynamics simulation approaches.
papers.abstract: The Oropouche virus (OROV) is an emerging zoonotic orthobunyavirus responsible for recurring outbreaks of febrile illness and neurological disorders in South and Central America. Despite its growing public health issues, no FDA-approved vaccines or antiviral therapies currently exist. To address this gap, a multiepitope subunit vaccine was designed to target OROV glycoproteins G1 (Gn), G2 (Gc), and the nucleocapsid (N) protein using a reverse-vaccinology (RV) approach. For vaccine construction, suitable epitopes (MHC-I, MHC-II, and linear B-cell) were selected based on percentile rank, antigen
papers.summary: This study uses reverse vaccinology and immunoinformatics to design a multiepitope subunit vaccine against Oropouche virus, targeting its glycoproteins G1, G2, and nucleocapsid protein. The authors identified MHC-I, MHC-II, and B-cell epitopes, then validated the construct through molecular docking and immune/dynamics simulations. The work provides an in silico vaccine candidate for a virus with no approved countermeasures.

papers.title: Immunoinformatics-based design of a multi-epitope mRNA vaccine candidate targeting the major human-infecting hepatitis E virus genotypes 1-4.
papers.abstract: Hepatitis E virus (HEV) is one of the leading causes of acute and chronic hepatitis among humans across the globe and is linked to severe diseases in immunocompromised individuals and pregnant women. Despite its substantial global burden, only one vaccine is licensed (in China and Pakistan), limiting its global accessibility. Furthermore, no globally approved mRNA vaccine against HEV is currently available, highlighting the need to develop strategies for alternative vaccines.
papers.summary: This study uses immunoinformatics approaches to design a multi-epitope mRNA vaccine candidate that targets the four major human-infecting hepatitis E virus genotypes (1-4). The authors computationally identified and combined B-cell and T-cell epitopes from conserved viral proteins to create a construct intended to provide broad genotype coverage, addressing the lack of a globally approved HEV mRNA vaccine.

papers.title: Computational identification of natural CXCR4-binding candidates relevant to endometriosis and ovarian cancer progression.
papers.abstract: Endometriosis and ovarian cancer share invasive, inflammatory, and pro-survival mechanisms in which CXCR4 signaling may play an important role, yet phytochemical modulators of this receptor remain insufficiently characterized. This study addressed that gap by integrating receptor reconstruction, ligand-guided docking, pharmacokinetic and toxicity prediction, pharmacophore mapping, density functional theory, replicated membrane-embedded molecular dynamics, and MM/GBSA analysis. A native human CXCR4 model was generated using SWISS-MODEL with 98.2% template coverage and 100% sequence identity, wh
papers.summary: This study computationally screened natural phytochemicals for their ability to bind CXCR4, a receptor implicated in both endometriosis and ovarian cancer progression. Using docking, pharmacokinetic/toxicity prediction, pharmacophore mapping, DFT, and membrane-embedded molecular dynamics with MM/GBSA, the authors identified candidate natural compounds with favorable binding and drug-like properties. The work provides a computational foundation for developing plant-derived CXCR4 modulators, though experimental validation is still needed.

papers.title: Investigating the anticancer potential of phytochemicals from the mangrove Rhizophora mucronata as inhibitors of lung cancer-associated proteins: Insights from multiscale computational and in silico analyses.
papers.abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, with a five-year survival rate of approximately 20-25% despite advances in targeted therapy and immunotherapy. There is a continuous need for novel, low-toxicity compounds capable of modulating key oncogenic pathways in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Mangrove ecosystems are rich reservoirs of bioactive phytochemicals, yet the inhibitory potential of compounds from Rhizophora mucronata against validated lung cancer-associated proteins has not been systematically explored using multi-scale computational approaches.
papers.summary: This study uses computational docking and simulation methods to screen phytochemicals from the mangrove plant Rhizophora mucronata as potential inhibitors of proteins linked to lung cancer. The authors identify candidate compounds that may bind key oncogenic targets in non-small cell lung cancer, suggesting these natural products warrant further experimental testing. The work is entirely in silico and does not include laboratory validation.

papers.title: A computational-first proof-of-concept for dual-function metal chelation and aggregate neutralization in an Aβ42 Drosophila model.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology is amplified by a self-reinforcing metal-Aβ-ROS axis, in which redox-active Cu and Fe bound to Aβ N-terminal histidines catalyze Fenton-like ROS generation and accelerate aggregation. Existing single-target interventions - anti-amyloid antibodies, antioxidants, metal-protein attenuating compounds, aggregation inhibitors, and photooxygenation catalysts - each address only one node of this loop. We used a computational-first framework to evaluate a dual-function strategy targeting two connected points of the axis: upstream redox-active metal sequestration by ma
papers.summary: This study uses a computational-first approach to design a dual-function molecule that both chelates redox-active metals (Cu, Fe) and neutralizes Aβ42 aggregates, targeting two connected nodes of the metal-Aβ-ROS axis in Alzheimer's disease. The strategy is validated as a proof-of-concept in a Drosophila Aβ42 model, showing that simultaneously addressing metal sequestration and aggregation may be more effective than single-target interventions.

papers.title: Systems-level analysis uncovers eight hub genes and a resveratrol-based therapeutic strategy for ischemic stroke.
papers.abstract: Ischemic stroke is a leading cause of mortality and long-term disability worldwide, yet its underlying molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. The pathology involves complex interactions between vascular injury, immune dysregulation, metabolic imbalance, and mitochondrial dysfunction. Traditional single-gene or single-dataset approaches have limitations in capturing the multifactorial nature of the disease. We developed a comprehensive systems-level bioinformatics framework integrating five publicly available transcriptomic datasets (GSE119121, GSE146882, GSE22255, GSE37587, GSE58
papers.summary: This study integrates five public transcriptomic datasets from ischemic stroke patients to identify eight hub genes through systems-level network analysis. The authors then propose resveratrol as a potential therapeutic strategy targeting these hub genes. The work highlights the multifactorial molecular landscape of ischemic stroke and suggests a drug repurposing avenue.

papers.title: Multi-omics identification of novel biomarkers and therapeutic targets for Parkinson's disease: from transcriptome to drug interaction.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder with limited therapeutic options. Acupuncture may serve as a complementary intervention, but its molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomic datasets to identify PD-associated diagnostic candidate genes and explore their relationship with acupuncture-related temporal expression patterns.
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk and single-cell transcriptomic datasets to identify candidate diagnostic genes for Parkinson's disease and explores how their expression patterns relate to acupuncture treatment. It aims to link transcriptome-derived biomarkers with potential drug interactions and therapeutic targets, positioning acupuncture as a complementary intervention.

papers.title: Nanozymes in Tumor Microenvironment Modulation for Cancer Therapy.
papers.abstract: The tumor microenvironment (TME) plays a central regulatory role in malignant tumor progression and therapeutic resistance, and its complexity and dynamic heterogeneity markedly limit the efficacy of current treatment strategies. Therefore, the development of novel functional materials capable of effectively remodeling the TME and alleviating immunosuppression and therapeutic tolerance has become an important research direction in cancer therapy. In recent years, nanozymes, as a class of nanomaterials with enzyme-mimicking catalytic activity, have shown broad potential in TME intervention and
papers.summary: This review discusses how nanozymes—nanomaterials that mimic natural enzyme activity—can be used to remodel the tumor microenvironment and overcome therapeutic resistance in cancer. It highlights the potential of these catalytic nanomaterials to alleviate immunosuppression and improve treatment outcomes, positioning them as a promising direction for next-generation cancer therapy.

papers.title: Structure-based virtual screening identifies ethyl rosmarinate as a SLC1A6-targeted therapeutic candidate for bladder cancer.
papers.abstract: SLC1A6 remains poorly characterized in bladder cancer. This study investigated its expression pattern, clinical relevance, cellular localization, functional implications, and potential pharmacological modulation.
papers.summary: This study characterizes SLC1A6 in bladder cancer, showing its expression pattern, clinical relevance, and cellular localization, and uses structure-based virtual screening to identify ethyl rosmarinate as a potential SLC1A6-targeted therapeutic candidate. The findings suggest SLC1A6 as a druggable target in bladder cancer and provide a lead compound for further development.

papers.title: Structure-based multi-pocket virtual screening identifies FDA-approved candidate compounds targeting MPXV thymidylate kinase.
papers.abstract: Mpox, caused by monkeypox virus (MPXV), has emerged as a growing global health concern, yet effective targeted antiviral therapies remain limited. Thymidylate kinase (TMK), an essential enzyme required for viral DNA replication, represents a potential therapeutic target.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study uses structure-based virtual screening against multiple pockets of the monkeypox virus thymidylate kinase (TMK), an essential enzyme for viral DNA replication, to identify potential antiviral drug candidates. The authors screened FDA-approved compounds and identified candidates that bind TMK, offering a repurposing strategy for mpox treatment.

papers.title: Discovery of Galangin Derivatives as a Potential T-cell Leukemia Virus 1 Protease Inhibitor Through Chemoinformatics Approaches
papers.summary: This study uses computational chemoinformatics methods to identify galangin derivatives as potential inhibitors of the T-cell leukemia virus 1 (HTLV-1) protease. Through virtual screening and molecular modeling, the authors propose these natural product analogs as promising lead compounds for antiviral development. The work is purely computational and lacks experimental validation.

papers.title: p70S6K as a Potential Anti-COVID-19 Target: Insights from Wet Bench and In Silico Studies
papers.abstract: The onset of SARS-CoV-2 infection in 2019 sparked a global COVID-19 pandemic. This infection is marked by a significant rise in both viral and host kinase activity. Our primary objective was to identify a pivotal host kinase essential for COVID-19 infection and the associated phenomenon of the cytokine storm, which may lead to long-term COVID-19 complications irrespective of viral genetic variations. To achieve this, our study tracked kinase phosphorylation dynamics in RAW264.7 macrophages following SPIKE transfection over time. Among the kinases surveyed, p70S6K (RPS6KB1) exhibited a 3.5-fold
papers.summary: The study tracked kinase phosphorylation dynamics in RAW264.7 macrophages after SPIKE transfection and identified p70S6K (RPS6KB1) as a host kinase showing a 3.5-fold increase in activity, suggesting it plays a pivotal role in COVID-19 infection and the cytokine storm. Combining wet bench experiments with in silico analyses, the authors propose p70S6K as a potential anti-COVID-19 therapeutic target that could be effective regardless of viral genetic variations.
